text: Your child has a fever. When should you worry?
Most parents get this wrong — what is it?
Most parents start with the cough syrup. That is the wrong first step.
The first step is not medicine. It is the thermometer, and a pen.
Write down the number and the time. You will need both tonight.
How often, and how high?
A parent called me and said, "He has a fever and a dry cough."
That morning it was thirty-eight point five. A little high.
Check it every four hours, and write down each number.
So what are the three things to do tonight?
One: give the medicine twice a day, after every meal.
Two: warm honey water, small cups all day. It helps a dry cough.
Three: he should have a good rest. No running for two days, no PE.
Open the window for ten minutes after dinner. Keep the room warm.
Most of it you already have at home. That is the good news.
If the fever goes above thirty-nine, call me the same day.
And if it rises at night, go to the hospital immediately.
Twice a day, every four hours, and thirty-nine means the hospital.
Right. And a good rest. That is the part parents forget.
Thank you, Dr. Lee. See you next time.
